terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where Idris's price list says what to do with each paper count when it arrives.

tasks.title: Callbacks that wait
tasks.description:
Implement `then(onFulfilled, onRejected)` in `src/docket.js` for a docket that is still pending.

- `then()` keeps both callbacks and returns; nothing runs yet
- when the docket is kept, `onFulfilled(value)` runs, with the docket's very value
- when it fails, `onRejected(reason)` runs instead
- only the matching callback runs, and only once, however often `resolve` is called

`then()` does not need to return anything yet. The check calls `then()` on pending dockets of its own, settles them, and records which callback ran, how often and with what.
nextSteps: Run `node src/price-list.js` and read the error.
Give the docket somewhere to keep callbacks until it settles.
When the docket settles, run what was kept.
Run the script: the card lines should appear after the rest of the script.
hints: When `then()` is called on a pending docket, the value does not exist yet. All `then()` can do is remember what to do with it.
The code that knows the moment the docket settles is the shared function behind `resolve` and `reject`. A list on the docket can carry the callbacks from `then()` to there.
In `then()`, push a small function onto `this.waiting` that runs `onFulfilled(this.value)` or `onRejected(this.value)` by the state. After settling, run every function in the list.

tasks.title: A docket that already has its value
tasks.description:
Make `then()` work on a docket that has already settled.

- on a docket already kept, `onFulfilled(value)` runs
- on a docket already failed, `onRejected(reason)` runs
- each `then()` runs its own callback once

The check calls `then()` on dockets of its own that settled inside the executor or a moment before, and records which callback ran and with what. The callback may run at once or a moment later.
nextSteps: Look at the posters line in the price list: that docket is kept before `then()` is called.
Think about what will settle that docket later. Nothing will.
Look at the state in `then()` and act on it.
Run the script: the posters line should appear.
hints: A docket can be asked for its value long after it arrived. The callbacks you keep are only run when the docket settles, and a settled docket never settles again.
`then()` can see `this.state`. When it is not `'pending'`, there is nothing to wait for.
Keep the callback only when the state is `'pending'`; otherwise run the same small function at once.

tasks.title: Many callbacks, and missing ones
tasks.description:
Make `then()` work when it is called many times, or without both callbacks.

- every `then()` on one docket gets its turn: all callbacks run, in the order the `then()` calls were made, each once, whether they were added before the docket settled or after
- a callback that is missing, `null` or not a function is skipped without an error

This task builds on tasks 1 and 2; the check says so when one of them is not done. It calls `then()` several times on dockets of its own, some with a callback missing or a string in its place, and records what ran.
nextSteps: Look at the two `then()` calls on card in the price list.
Make sure a new callback never takes the place of one already waiting.
Check that a callback is a function before you call it.
Run the script: both card lines should appear, in order.
hints: One docket can have many readers. Each `then()` is one of them, and none of them may be forgotten.
A list keeps things in the order they were added if you add at the end and run from the start. `typeof x === 'function'` tells you whether something can be called.
Push each new callback onto the end of the list, run the list with a `for...of` loop, and call a callback only when `typeof callback === 'function'`.
